task.description: Produce design artefact(s) for 4 MUST requirements from docs/requirements.yaml (stage 16): DDL-02 (cross-statement ordering check, extends DDL-01's ValidatePlatformDDL -- rejects a migration file set that constrains a column before it exists/is backfilled, e.g. SET NOT NULL / ADD CONSTRAINT without NOT VALID / ADD COLUMN NOT NULL without a default appearing before the expand+backfill statements it depends on), ORD-01 (effect-completion claim via SELECT...FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED against a new plat_effect_completion table), ORD-02 (per-correlation advisory-lock execute guard: pg_try_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(correlation_id)::bigint), false result rolls back without incrementing retry), ORD-04 (per-correlation parallelism + lag observability via a new plat_correlation_cursor table, exposing max(sequence_no)-applied_seq lag, oldest-pending-row age, and execute-guard false-rate). Read the full requirement bodies directly from docs/requirements.yaml (yaml.safe_load, utf-8-sig) -- read ALL acceptance criteria carefully, this preview only showed the first sentence of each. CRITICAL: this is SUBSTANTIALLY NEW subsystem work -- grep confirms no plat_effect_completion or plat_correlation_cursor tables/code exist anywhere yet (only mentioned as naming-convention examples in DDL-05's design doc). You must design the full new schema (Type C) for both tables from scratch, following DDL-05's plat_ namespace convention (both table names already start with plat_, correctly). Read src/platform/ddl_validate.zig (DDL-01, to extend for DDL-02) and src/platform/ddl_namespace.zig in full before designing DDL-02. For ORD-01/02/04, check if any existing consumer/worker-polling pattern exists elsewhere in this codebase (e.g. timer/DLQ processing, webhook delivery) to follow established conventions for FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED polling loops and advisory-lock usage -- do not invent a new pattern if one already exists.
acceptance_criteria: Every acceptance criterion in DDL-02, ORD-01, ORD-02, ORD-04 is covered by the design
DDL-02 explicitly extends src/platform/ddl_validate.zig's ValidatePlatformDDL rather than creating a parallel validator
New plat_effect_completion and plat_correlation_cursor tables designed as Type C migration(s), following the plat_ reserved namespace correctly
ORD-01/02/04 design cites any existing polling/advisory-lock convention in this codebase it follows, or explicitly notes none exists and justifies the new pattern

result.summary: Design artefacts for 4 Stage-16 MUST requirements (DDL-02, ORD-01, ORD-02, ORD-04). DDL-02 is a Type E extension to src/platform/ddl_validate.zig's ValidatePlatformDDL pipeline (new checkConstrainBeforeExpand whole-file-scan check, a fourth check composed alongside the existing lock-class/index-concurrency/namespace checks, not a parallel validator). ORD-01/02/04 decompose into 2 Type C migration YAMLs (plat_effect_completion, plat_correlation_cursor -- confirmed via grep that neither table exists anywhere in src/ or migrations/ before this batch) plus 1 Type E design for the novel BPM Consumer polling+advisory-lock orchestration logic. The existing src/effects/worker.zig + src/effects/queue.zig (EXP-301 effects outbox) polling pattern was found and followed for connection acquisition, FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claim shape, and typed-error philosophy. ORD-02's per-correlation advisory lock is explicitly distinguished from the scheduler's ISS-301 removed per-timer advisory lock (that lock was redundant with SKIP LOCKED on the same row; ORD-02's lock guards a different row of the same correlation, which SKIP LOCKED cannot do). The design is written to be compatible with ORD-03 (order guard + cursor advance + gap sweeper), which is out of this batch's scope but shares both new tables -- an explicit applyFn extension point and a stub (stubAlwaysDeferred) are specified so this batch's consumer loop can be wired safely before ORD-03 lands without misapplying anything. All 4 artefacts pass tools/lint_design_artefact.py with 0 issues; both migration YAMLs pass codegen_migration.py --dry-run with exit 0.
